description: Re-poses the a_K operator-selection LP on H_n/rad (the blocks convention D leaves alive) and asks whether that recovers a_K. It makes y0* nonzero and a_K defined, but does NOT recover a_K — and the convention-C history shows the LP never did, missing by up to 1.6e17 ppm. audit_only; no anchor, no fit.
tier: structural-exact (decidable; LP optimum is an argmin, no fit)

result.verdict: Quotient restriction makes a_K DEFINED but does NOT recover it: worst |quotient vs closed| = 1.939e+10 ppm. The LP reduces to y0* = min_i |contrib_i| (verified on all 6 atoms), so the dual carries no operator-selection content. Convention C missed by up to 1.6e17 ppm, so this is NOT a convention-D regression — D turned a wrong number into no number. Scope-(a): refutes the LP AS POSED (t = |contrib| against a sum-to-target constraint); does NOT exclude an operator-selection LP as the route to a_K.
result.trace_constraint_note: aK_via_lp_dual_full documents 'Σ_λ contrib_λ·x_λ = tr_M_atom (reproduce trace)' but the solver enforces Σ_λ x_λ = n_target. The contributions enter the objective only, so trace reproduction has never been a constraint, under either convention. Not repaired here — it changes what the probe means.

convention_C_history.note: from the committed convention-C witness, before this campaign; a_K^dual vs a_K^closed
